title: Mop and Flicker's Nap Adventure
markdown:
High up in the Candlecap Mountains, where the air smelled of soft moss and pinecones, lived a little goblin named Mop. Mop was not the sort of goblin who liked to stomp and roar. He was kind, with eyes the colour of new leaves, and his nose would wiggle like a busy beetle when he thought hard. The thing Mop thought about most was Flicker.

Flicker was a marmot, round and fluffy, the colour of a dandelion. His tail was like a happy question mark, and his very favourite thing in the whole wide world was a good long nap. Flicker had a very special place for those naps. The grass had to be soft as a whisper. The sunbeams had to feel like warm butter. And it had to be close to the big flat grey rock that stayed warm all afternoon. Today Flicker felt very sleepy. His little paws wanted to go to his special nap place.

“Time for a nap, Flicker?” Mop asked, his voice as soft as a butterfly’s wing.

Flicker made a tiny squeak, like a little bell. Mop knew that squeak.

“Let’s find your favourite nap spot, then. The glowworm glade is lovely this morning, and it’s near those big rocks you like.”

Holding hands, Mop and Flicker walked. The sun was just waking, painting the sky soft pink and gold. Little boots crunched on the path, kicking up tiny puffs of damp earth. They walked toward the glowworm glade, where tiny lights twinkled like little stars even in the daytime. Close to the big rocks Flicker loved for snoozing. Sleepy bees. Sweet wild thyme.

As they walked, Mop saw someone near a bush full of the plumpest reddest berries. Elderberry, an elf. Hair as if woven with sunshine. A shiny green tunic. A basket full of bright red berries that looked like jewels. She was reaching for a very big berry, looking very focused.

“Hello, Mop,” Elderberry called, voice like little bells. “And who is this sleepy fellow with you? He looks as if he’s dreaming of naps.”

“Hello, Elderberry. This is Flicker. He needs to find his special nap spot before his eyes get too heavy.”

Elderberry’s eyes sparkled.

“Oh, I know just the place for a marmot who loves his naps.” She pointed with a twig that had a tiny leaf on it, toward a path with patches of sunshine, into a patch of flowers that looked as if they were giggling. “It’s just past those giggling flowers. Follow that path, and you’ll see the softest moss.”

Mop and Flicker walked along the path. Flicker stopped sometimes to sniff an interesting root. Elderberry, who had followed a little way behind to show them the exact turn, stopped very suddenly. Her nose was almost touching the biggest reddest berry she had ever seen.

“Oh my goodness. Look at this one. Round as a button and red as a robin’s chest. It smells like sunshine.”

She forgot all about showing them the way. She was too busy picking the best berries, eyes shining with the joy of finding such perfect ones.

Mop waited kindly. He knew Flicker’s nap time was very important. He also knew Elderberry loved her berries very much. He watched her with a gentle smile. Then he looked up at the sky. Sunbeams slanted through the tall trees, golden stripes on the forest floor. The biggest stripe was falling right onto a patch of soft moss, next to the biggest flattest grey rock he knew. That was when he remembered. Flicker liked to nap where the sunbeams tickled his nose, but not too much. Usually by that big flat grey rock that felt like a giant sleeping cat. Softest moss, where the sunbeams kissed it.

“Thank you, Elderberry. Your berries are very beautiful. But I think I remember now. Flicker likes the warm rock best.”

Elderberry blinked. She wiped a little berry juice from her fingers and looked up from her treasure.

“Oh dear.” Cheeks a soft pink. “I do love berries, don’t I? Sorry, Mop. Sometimes the best ones just catch my eye. But yes, you’re right.” She pointed with a berry-stained finger, not to the giggling flowers, but to a different spot. “That big flat rock over there is often the warmest. And look.”

Right beside the big flat grey rock, where the sunbeams were a gentle golden blanket, was Flicker’s very favourite nap spot. Grass soft as a cloud. Moss thick and inviting. Sunbeams just right, warm and gentle on his fluffy fur. Flicker let out a happy sigh. He curled into a perfect little sunshine ball, question-mark tail tucked neatly around him. He was fast asleep before Mop could hum another note. As snug as a bug in a warm sunny rug.

Elderberry giggled, little bells dancing.

“He looks so cozy. A perfect marmot slumber.” She opened her basket. “Would you like some berries, Mop? They are very sweet, picked just now.”

Mop smiled a big goblin smile that crinkled his leaf-green eyes.

“Yes, please.”

And so Mop sat happily with Elderberry, sharing sweet juicy berries that tasted like sunshine. Flicker dreamed of warm naps and fluffy clouds in his perfect spot. Mop did not need a speech about remembering. He had remembered the rock. The marmot was already asleep on it. That was the afternoon, and it was enough.
